editorial.brief: Lizzie Borden led Wikipedia with 421,359 views, only 1.1 times the count for Ted Kaczynski, and no topic crossed a second feed today. The largest of 25 quakes was an M5.6 off Papua New Guinea, and the US and Iran ceasefire market sits at 87 percent.
editorial.cover_sub: Lizzie Borden took the top Wikipedia spot on a day when no story crossed a second feed, ahead of Ted Kaczynski by a margin thin enough to need a steward's inquiry.
editorial.wiki_deck: Lizzie Borden drew 421,359 views, ahead of Ted Kaczynski at 376,033 and Roblox at 370,335. Nothing else in the snapshot says why.
editorial.letter_headline: A Sunday of no shared subject
editorial.discourse_deck: Hacker News wants better tools, led by a NewPipe fork at 360 points. Lemmy wants memes and old memories, Bluesky a meat-raffle win, Mastodon a colourful sky and some grumbling about AI executives.
editorial.foreign_deck: The wire ran Anthropic's CEO asking the industry to slow down, while Brazil and Britain searched for Norma Dumont and Ailín Pérez, and Japan for the Toyota Noah.
editorial.markets_deck: Two markets carried $1M: Minnesota against Washington at 77 percent yes, and the US and Iran ceasefire holding through September 30 at 87. Hormuz traffic normalising sits at zero.
editorial.watch_deck: Steam supplied only app numbers: 730 peaked at 1,354,009 players, 570 at 875,875. On Twitch, TheBurntPeanut led with 39,977 viewers, ahead of 加藤純一うん〇ちゃん at 32,021 and xQc at 31,134.
editorial.yt_headline: Taylor Swift, in lyric video form
editorial.yt_note: WERWULF's trailer leads on views at 3,865,615, ahead of Minecraft LIVE at 3,320,095 and the Taylor Swift lyric video at 1,930,773. The Musk trailer sits last with 30,257.
editorial.closing_note: Gone by tomorrow: Lizzie Borden's 421,359 views, the M5.6 near Kokopo, TheBurntPeanut's 39,977 viewers and the 87 percent on a ceasefire question that runs to September 30. The medal table will carry new numbers, and google's birthday will return next year.
wiki_paras: Lizzie Borden topped Wikipedia's most-read list with 421,359 views. Ted Kaczynski followed at 376,033 and Roblox at 370,335, so the top three sit within about 51,000 views of one another. The lead over second place is 1.1 times, which is a lead in the way a nose is a lead at Ascot.

Nothing else in the snapshot accounts for it. No feed carries a Borden item, a Kaczynski item or a Roblox item, so the readers arrived with their own reasons and did not leave a note. The fourth and fifth places belong to one event, the Asian Games, with India's page at 260,257 and the medal table at 259,696.

Combined, the two Asian Games pages reach 519,953 views, more than any single page on the list. That makes the Games the largest block of attention of the day, though split across two headlines, while Borden takes the prize for the largest single page. Sundays are generous with such technicalities.
letter_paras: The snapshot found a scattered day. No topic crossed feeds, so Wikipedia read about Lizzie Borden, Hacker News about a SponsorBlock fork of NewPipe, and the AI wire about Anthropic's CEO urging slower model development. Each feed kept its own counsel, and the only agreement was that nothing needed agreeing upon.

Two small details. On Hugging Face, an uncensored GGUF version of Qwen-Image-2.1 has 876,673 downloads, against 48,361 for the Qwen release, and a model called laya has none. In Google Trends, the United States searched for google's birthday, which is Google being asked to recall its own age.

A same-hour snapshot fixes one moment across seventeen feeds, so a topic that appears in several counts as coincidence rather than drift. Repeat it daily and the ordinary days build a baseline, against which a genuinely odd one shows up without needing to shout. Today's baseline entry reads: scattered.
